findings: `learner.overview.text` presents the direct-numeral and borrowed-graph accounts too vaguely to distinguish their evidence. Revise it to say that early forms written 亖 directly represented four and coexisted with forms written 四 (X-e6d62080b1a5fc5178a4); the counting-rod explanation is a separate interpretation of some 四 forms (X-7b17032f87fb77433387). Keep the two borrowing proposals distinct: one treats 四 as a breath-related graph associated with 呬, later borrowed for four, without establishing the depicted referent’s ancient name (X-2723cf5f9190c41c2cfe, X-4b62255296f832195814); the other proposes 四 was the original graph for 泗, depicting nasal discharge, later borrowed for four, and lacks textual attestation (X-e6d62080b1a5fc5178a4). Retain the current 囗-around-儿-form description as visible structure only (X-741838c69c6335267eb0).
